name: DEMOCRACY
description: Democracy is a unique trick-taking game for 2-6 players where all players simultaneously select and reveal cards. The game features a colonial backstory where players represent powers attempting to annex an island. Cards have special rankings (5-4-3-A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6) and point values, with the goal of capturing majority points in suits to score 'tribes'.

content.text: Democracy is a unique trick-taking game for 2-6 players where all players simultaneously select and reveal cards. The game features a colonial backstory where players represent powers attempting to annex an island. Cards have special rankings (5-4-3-A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6) and point values, with the goal of capturing majority points in suits to score 'tribes'.

Country/Region of Origin: Cleveland, Ohio, USA
Time Period: 2004 or earlier
Historical Development: Played at the Tabletop Board Game Cafe in Cleveland. Unknown whether invented there or introduced from elsewhere.
Cultural Significance: Part of a unique gaming culture in Cleveland along with related game 'Ribs'

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 3-5
Partnerships: None - individual play

Type: Modified standard deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Added for 4 players (2 jokers), 6 players (1 joker)
Card removal: All twos removed (48 cards base)
Special ranking: 5-4-3-A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6 (high to low)

Standard 52-card deck
Score sheet for tracking tribes
Table space for voting pool

Cards dealt face down clockwise
Extra 'voting pool' hand dealt to center
Two-day structure: half deck each day (or play variations)
Example: 4 players = 5 cards each + 5 in pool per day

items.text: Days: Play the whole game as a single day, or divide into more than two days; more days means less choice and more luck.
Bad Catch: Player dealt only one-point cards in first day may call misdeal and score one tribe automatically.
High Stake: Bad-catch player may elect high stake; suits they win score 2 (or 3) tribes instead of 1.
Ghost / Klepto: When joker is voting card, each player draws one card from neighbour's hand and captures it; joker discarded.
Dummy Joker: Joker worth zero, ranks below 6, always loses; no suit.
Suit Sweep: Player capturing all 12 cards of a suit scores two tribes; some require announcing sweep before first vote.
